summary: Hidemasa Nagata (1933–2024) was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1953 to 1962 and later held a post there from circa 1968 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at Tokyo, Kyoto University (1920, 1931–1946), and Kyoto Women's University (~1958–1974).

Hidenori Kitagawa (1920–1969) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hakuju Ui. He served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969) and taught Musashi Tachikawa and Kōken Unno.

Hidenori S. Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, later serving at Shitennoji University and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Taisho University and Waseda University, where he taught as a lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1968–1998), before serving as a professor at Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1997–2003).

Hideomi Yaita is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University around 1979–1984, served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1986–1997), and lectured at Taisho University in 1995.
Hidetaka Fukazawa is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from 1975 to 1979 and held a post at Hitotsubashi University from around 1992 to 2021.
Hideto Ono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2008) and as a chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), where he later taught Arthur Waley. He held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), Osaka University (~1932–1946), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and the University of Tokyo (~1946).

Hideyo Ogawa is an Indology, philosophy, and linguistics scholar. He taught Shindo Kusumoto and served at Hiroshima University as an associate professor (attested 1991) and as a professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2009–2013, 2026).

Hideyuki Matsumori is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006) and later served there as an assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Himanshu Prabha Ray is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at Panjab, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. She was an associate professor at JNU (~1980–2012) and served as chairperson of the National Monuments Authority (~2012–2015).

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a religious studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810), held a post at the University of Breslau (~1815–1861), and taught Albrecht Weber.

Hiram W. Woodward is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and Yale. He taught at the University of Michigan (1972–1982) and the University of Vermont (~1982–1986), then served as Asian art curator at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri (1878–1946) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at DAV College and Oriental College. He worked with the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, and served as Director of Archaeology for Baroda (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1961–1966). He held posts at Tohoku University as a lecturer (attested 1972) and associate professor (attested 1989–2000), and at Shimane University (attested 1974).

Hirofumi Toda (1936–2003) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University (attested 1985–1999) and held a post at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of Lotus Sutra (attested 1985).

Hiroko Kawanami is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. She taught Shi Jiancheng and served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).

Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and later held posts at the University of Leipzig (attested 2016) and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).
